scope: A schedule using only the modulus gives at least 2/t success per run of the chosen ForShor circuit, using t = 64(1+floor(log₂(1+floor(log₂N)))). The bound comes from its matrix recovery theorem with κ=1/π².
The allocated compiled circuit measures a clock of size 2^floor(log₂(2N²)). This specifies the physical input to the decoder; the ideal paper-clock theorem separately uses N²≤Q<2N².
The known-N schedule has failure at most exp(−2) < 1/3 under the actual product of independent compiled-circuit Born laws. Those tuple weights sum to one.

Every decoded denominator fits the clock. Streaming the records through bit-level decoding, a zero check, and a minimum selector agrees exactly with the reference minimum of the nonzero verified estimates, with all those data-path operations counted.

The physical bounded-error statement uses the executable Boolean decoder and streaming minimum on fresh zero-state preparations of the same compiled order-finding circuit. The number of preparations is determined from the known modulus.

Across the complete known-modulus repetition schedule for a valid unit input, the allocated circuit uses O(L⁴) logical gate operations and the decoder plus aggregation use ≤40,000,000 L⁵ Boolean data-path operations at sufficiently large input width L. These are loose upper bounds in the stated cost models.

Shor §§3–5. The normalized ideal paper-clock experiment has one-shot success ≥(4/π²)φ(r)/r and constant error after O(log log r) independent shots. A concrete compiled circuit, run for a count computed solely from N, yields the exact order with error <1/3 after Boolean decoding and aggregation. Total logical gates and classical data-path operations are polynomial in the bit length of N, with the distinct ideal and compiled clocks explicit.
